svg.title: Step flashing and kick-out flashing at a roof-to-wall joint
svg.desc: A roof running into the side of a two-story wall, with the siding cut away. Ice and water shield turns up the wall a few inches. An L-shaped piece of step flashing goes in with every course of shingles: one leg on the roof under the next shingle, one leg up the wall, each piece lapping the one below. At the bottom, where the eave meets the wall, a kick-out flashing turns the water out and into the gutter so it cannot run down behind the siding. The housewrap laps over the flashing legs and the siding goes on over that, held up off the roof. Illustration, not a photo of an actual job. Layer thicknesses are exaggerated so each one can be seen.
svg.text: HOW IT’S BUILT · ROOF MEETS WALL
Step flashing every course. Kick-out at the end.

g.text: 5 in on the roof, 5 in up the wall
